D.blurb: Ask questions about a table in plain English. The agent finds the table, writes read-only SQL, runs it and explains the result.
D.data: public.foods, 5,000 generated rows across 8 food categories (created in the notebook)
how: aidb.agent_converse with a conversation_id for follow-ups
q: What is the average calorie count of vegetarian foods by category?
D.learn: An agent discovers tables at question time. Every step is logged in ordinary tables.

D.blurb: Index a schema, not the data, so an agent can find tables, work out joins and answer in conversation.
D.data: banking schema: 6 tables with comments (7 branches, 15 customers, 25 accounts, ~50 transactions, 15 loans, ~30 payments)
how: Agent with 5 tools: semantic_kb_search, search_by_comment, list_relationships, find_join_path, run_sql_query
q: Which customers have delinquent loans and what is their total outstanding balance?
Which current one has the largest balance? (follow-up)
Which branches hold the highest total deposit balances?
Which accounts are overdrawn, and who owns them?
Which transactions were flagged as fraud, and which customers do they belong to?
What is the total outstanding loan balance by loan type, and by region?
D.learn: Comments on tables and columns drive search quality. Editing a comment changes what the agent finds.

D.blurb: Two knowledge bases, a table and two PDFs, and one agent that picks the right source for each question.
D.data: public.food_notes (12 notes) and two IRS PDFs: i1040gi.pdf and p17.pdf
how: AI pipeline: KnowledgeBase for the table; ParsePdf, ChunkText, KnowledgeBase for PDFs
Custom SQL tools search_food and search_tax_docs
PGFS storage location and volume, pgfs.allowed_local_fs_paths
q: What should I eat to build muscle?
What are the new rules for overtime?
What are the new rules for taxes on tips?
D.learn: Same recipe for any source: pipeline, similarity search, custom tool, agent. Logging is automatic.

D.blurb: Two agents with identical instructions see different data, because each runs as a different database role.
D.data: cc_raw.credit_card_transactions, 100,000 sampled rows from Hugging Face pointe77/credit-card-transaction
how: View with column-level masking via pg_has_role
aidb.create_purpose, agents tied to a purpose
Semantic KB over the cc_demo schema
q: What are the top 10 states in terms of sum of credit card transactions? (supervisor answers, analyst cannot)
D.learn: Enforcement sits in the database. It applies to people, apps and agents alike.

D.blurb: Extract fields from customs PDFs with an agent, check them with plain SQL rules, then explain the findings.
D.data: 18 sample customs PDFs, 3 shipments with 6 documents each (Mexico to US auto parts)
D.net: None, but the PDFs must already be staged
how: Extraction agent with a 19-field typed output (aidb.output_type)
required_fields table (31 rules) and customs_findings view with 6 checks
q: Which shipments are ready to file and which are not?
What is wrong with shipment AB-2026-7731 and how do I fix it?
D.learn: The model only extracts. Rules stay in SQL, so they are exact and auditable. Expect findings only for AB-2026-7731.

D.blurb: Turn the agent conversation log into a knowledge base and put an agent on top of it.
D.data: public.aidb_conversations, built from aidb.conversation_log (run after the other demos)
q: What are the most common questions asked?
D.learn: Understand what users ask and where agents struggle. Most useful after the other demos have run.

D.blurb: Cap what an agent can spend, and see what happens when it hits the cap.
D.data: supply_chain schema, 16 tables (about 5,000 sales orders, 15,000 order lines, 1,500 PO lines)
how: aidb.update_agent with max_iterations and budget_strategy (error or summarize)
q: What are the tables available with this agent?
How many purchase orders are overdue?
Which is the largest one? (follow-up)
How many items are in each warehouse? (with a 2-iteration budget)
D.learn: Three levers drive cost: the model, the iteration cap and the token budgets.

D.blurb: Call an LLM from plain SQL, per row or aggregated across a group, with built-in or custom prompts.

Score sentiment of one review, then of a whole film
D.learn: Combine AI calls with WHERE, GROUP BY, joins and views. Each call hits the model, so filter first.

Q.q: What format is the AWS image: a machine image, a container image, or something else?
Q.a: Make the GitHub project open source. Users build their own image from detailed instructions that include getting an EDB Subscription Token, which lets us track installs. On AWS, use the same token with a provided CloudFormation template (see AIDB Quickstarts).

Q.q: Do we publish one full Docker image, or a full tag and a slim tag?
Which models do we bundle, and which are pulled on first use?
Q.a: Embeddings: local models. LLM: Claude, since the field has access to it and it gives the least friction for demos.

Q.q: Which phi-4 class model do we mean, and does it call tools reliably enough for the SQL analyst?
What eval licence terms cover the EDB components, the models and the sample data?
Q.a: The EULA allows a trial for internal demonstration, test or evaluation during the term of the offering. The get-your-token page says 60 days. Standard EULA and terms apply.
